For u!=0 put r=|u|, P_u=I-uu^T/r^2, phi(x)=pi cos^2(x)/(2[(pi/2)^2-x^2]^2) with removable values, and A_T^K(u)=int_|k|<=K (P_u k)(P_u k)^T |k|^-4 T phi(T k.u) dk. Positivity, evenness and exact transversality give the standard Landau weak-form conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy and entropy dissipation. Angular/radial elimination yields A_T^K=(pi/r)[log(KTr)-c+epsilon(KTr)]P_u, with 0<=epsilon(a)<=pi^2/(8a^2) and c=1/2+log(pi/2)-Ci(pi)-Si(pi)/pi. A value at u=0 is irrelevant only for the stated absolutely continuous weak interface.

Finite memory regularizes the infrared integral without supplying a screening length; the ultraviolet cutoff remains. At fixed L>0, the log-K-normalized weak generator tends to pi P_u/r under the specified density, score and logarithmic-tail hypotheses. It does not prove convergence of evolved laws or collisional-time iid particles. A discrete torus and a vanishing small-mode cutoff are separate obligations. For supplied Yukawa response, the cosine angular error is O(L^-2), uniform in finite K, with both bounded-score-Hessian and bounded-density/finite-Fisher weak variants. These assumptions are not acquired from microscopic dynamics.

At equal maximum time lag, cosine minimizes frequency variance only within the stated nonnegative squared-Fourier window class. Fejer windows also recover the same leading logarithm with finite absolute logarithmic moment. Cosine improves the variance and convergence rate, not existence of this limit; its matched unscreened offset is not uniformly superior. No molecular simulation, instrument, device or CPU advantage was demonstrated. The supplied radial infinite-time tensor already has a closed-form baseline.

The raw unprojected tensor retains b_T^K(r)=pi R_phi(KTr)/r: nonzero energy defect before log normalization, although subleading in that limit. Narrow Lorentzian response ridges force memory Omega(1/width). Neither projection nor a normalized limit permits exchanging all limits or discarding physical field/potential energy.

The companion exact pair ledger mu_N=(N-1) pushforward(f_2,N) under rho=N(x1-x2) tracks close-pair energy. Its fast-scale equation retains an explicit three-particle/external-force remainder. Smooth correlated dimer preparations approach independent fixed-order marginals yet change a bounded velocity observable in O(1/N); they defeat the unweighted restart interface, not the iid target. Rutherford covariance uses an additional independent-encounter flux. The shifted echo calculation is a prescribed-field diagnostic with every derivative and field amplitude retained, not a self-consistent plasma counterexample. Energy alone does not control grazing impulse covariance. The missing operation is acquisition and control of this weighted pair/history state from iid dynamics through N/log N time.
